To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the new dibenzofuranyl derivatives obtained in this work are promising antibacterial agents, especially against multiresistant Stapylococcus aureus.

the new polyoxygenated 2-methylbutilated dibenzofuran compounds are promising antibacterial agents with activity against multiresistant Gram-positive bacteria, and that a structure-activity relationship was established.
the introduction of two 2-methyl butyl chains on dibenzofuranes leads to a series of compounds with antibacterial activity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis and biological evaluation of new dibenzofurane derivatives.
the synthesis of a new series of dibenzofuranes with different substitution patterns and the evaluation of their activity against Gram-positive bacteria.

the synthesis and antibacterial activity evaluation of new polyoxygenated compounds, with special attention to dibenzofuranes, a family of compounds that have been reported as having antibacterial activity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the presence of a methyl butyl chain at C-2, C-6, or C-8 is important for the antibacterial activity of the dibenzofurane nucleus, and that the introduction of an oxygenated group at C-3, C-4 or C-5 is also important for this activity

the presence of a 2-methylpropyl chain at C-2 of the dibenzofuranes, as well as the presence of a hydroxyl group at C-4, are the main structural requisites for the activity of the synthesized compounds.
the antibacterial activity of these compounds is related to the number of oxygenated groups, the length and the position of the aliphatic chain, and the presence or not of the methoxyl group at C-2.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the presence of a methylbutyril moiety at the 2- or 8-positions of the aromatic ring is a structural requirement for the compounds to exhibit antibacterial activity.

the introduction of a methylbutyl chain at C-2 or C-8 of the dibenzofuran ring increases the antibacterial activity of the molecule, and the introduction of a second methylbutyl chain in the C-4 or C-6 position of the dibenzodioxine ring further increases the activity.
the presence of a methyl group at C-4 is important for activity and the presence of a hydroxyl group at C-3 is not essential.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the synthesis of polyoxygenated aromatic compounds is a feasible approach for the development of new antibiotics.
the presence of two methylbutyril chains at C-4, C-6, or C-2, C-8 of dibenzofurane is crucial to the antibacterial activity of these molecules.
it is possible to obtain new compounds with interesting biological activities through a sequence of simple reactions starting with commercial compounds.
